A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICBench/IGAR work. All 16 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of three VLA models across 30 LIBERO tasks, hyperparameter sensitivity results and a physical-robot demonstration.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds component-ablation results in Table 4 and inference-latency measurements in Section 5.4.

M1.justification: IGAR retains the same sink detection, grounding-head selection and attention redistribution procedures, equations and default parameters. The new component ablations evaluate reduced configurations without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 30 LIBERO Spatial, Object and Goal tasks, four contradiction types and Franka cube-placement scenario. The new ablation uses the existing LIBERO-Goal/ICBench V1 setting; timing measurements add no task or data coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 4 adds evaluated comparison configurations without sink detection, without head selection, and with detection only. The main π0, π0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT comparator set remains unchanged; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a component-toggle evaluation using π0.5 on LIBERO-Goal under ICBench V1, reporting attention-to-text alongside LGS, and per-step OpenVLA-OFT timing on an RTX 5090. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. The relationship between attention-to-text and v1's IVAR is unspecified.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 adds a focused component ablation testing whether sink detection, head selection and redistribution contribute beyond the baseline. This supplements the unchanged hyperparameter sensitivity analysis in Figure 4. Section 5.4 also adds an inference-cost analysis.

E5.justification: v2 reports 50 timing trials and latency values of 98.7±2.0 and 105.6±0.5 ms, introducing uncertainty reporting for this experiment without defining the ± statistic. The existing 50 independent rollouts per task variant remain unchanged; no uncertainty intervals are added to SR/LGS results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and all existing figure results are unchanged. Table 4 adds attention-to-text values and ablation LGS results, including 4.6 without sink detection and 4.2 without head selection. Its baseline/full-IGAR LGS values of 3.8/7.4 already appeared in Tables 1–2. Section 5.4 newly reports latency increasing from 98.7 to 105.6 ms with IGAR.

T1.justification: v2 removes the head-averaged attention and Instruction Visual Attention Ratio definitions from v1 Section 4.1, Equations 2–3. The LGS definition and IGAR equations remain substantively unchanged, with subsequent equations renumbered. No replacement mathematical definition is provided for attention-to-text.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal diagnosis, benchmark, intervention and performance-preservation claims. Section 2.2 adds an explicit priority claim that IGAR is the first inference-time intervention designed for VLA policies.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new component ablation as showing that IGAR's stages are complementary rather than redundant, and characterizes the measured latency overhead as modest. Existing interpretations of linguistic blindness, baseline preservation and real-world behavior remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and identifies the single NVIDIA RTX 5090 used for the new timing experiment. Existing implementation thresholds, layer settings and robot hardware descriptions are retained. The link alone does not establish code or data availability.

R1.justification: v2 retains the original references and adds six works concerning gaslighting, attention reallocation, robot trustworthiness and anomaly detection. Section 2.2 expands the gaslighting discussion and explicitly distinguishes IGAR from attention-sink mitigation for LLMs/MLLMs, adding a VLA-specific priority assertion.

P1.justification: Changes include localized grammar and paragraph edits, revised affiliations and running title, an acknowledgment, and expansion of Section 5.5's heading and discussion. The section order and most prose remain unchanged; there is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds the component-ablation Table 4 and rearranges retained displays, including placing Table 1 after its diagnostic discussion and Figure 4 after its sensitivity discussion. All five figure images and the contents of Tables 1–3 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The component ablation provides useful evidence about IGAR's design, while the latency measurement quantifies a previously unreported practical cost. These modest gains accompany unchanged main results. Reporting remains imperfect: v2 removes the IVAR definition while introducing undefined attention-to-text results, and does not explain the timing ± statistic.
